correctness.rationale: The twelve witnesses and the two exceptional lower bounds were independently reconstructed in exact arithmetic. For \(k=5\) and \(k=7\), a putative Fourier support at most three gives nine Fourier zeros. The exact-support kernel criterion is correct: a full-support kernel vector exists exactly when no coordinate functional vanishes identically on the kernel. Independent exact cyclotomic elimination reproduced the package census: after modular full-rank filters only 96 five-column and 1680 seven-column cases remain; every former has exact rank four, every latter exact rank six, and every one-dimensional kernel forces a zero time coordinate. Explicit exact witnesses attain Fourier support four. The other entries follow from the published monotone lower envelope and exact witnesses. Thus the finite classification is exhaustive, not sampled.

originality.rationale: Originality passes with an important qualification. Krahmer--Pfander--Rashkov already display a numerical \(\mathbb Z_{12}\) support-pair diagram and explicitly describe the underlying computations as numerical. That is prior numerical evidence for the same profile, so the values themselves are not a fresh numerical discovery. The audited result supplies a rigorous exact theorem: explicit exact witnesses plus a complete cyclotomic-rank obstruction proving that exact supports five and seven cannot have Fourier support at most three. No inspected primary source gives that exact proof. Bonami--Ghobber's proved equality classifications cover other group families, not \(\mathbb Z_{12}\).
